title: Thought Experiment
coreMove: Run a constrained mental simulation to expose hidden assumptions before reality charges the full price.
sourcePressure: The source frames thought experiments as structured mental simulations for impossible, costly, or not-yet-testable situations. It names Zeno, Descartes, Galileo, Laplace, Einstein, Plato, Wittgenstein, Ernst Mach, and the trolley problem lineage, but the plan should keep the method practical.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version treats any imaginative scenario as useful thinking.

sourceAnchors.name: Ernst Mach
sourceAnchors.detail: the source uses Mach to frame thought experiments as low-cost experimentation that often precedes physical experimentation
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Mach's point gives imagination a job: spend a few minutes in the mind before spending money in the world.

sourceAnchors.name: Einstein
sourceAnchors.detail: the source lists Einstein among historical anchors for thought experiments
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Einstein belongs here as a reminder that the best mental simulation is not loose fantasy; it is imagination held inside rules.

sourceAnchors.name: The trolley problem lineage
sourceAnchors.detail: the frozen source includes the trolley problem as an example of thought experiments in ethics
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The trolley problem lasts because a stripped-down scene can make a hidden moral rule show itself.

counterintuition: imagination is as good as evidence
tryThisNow: close your eyes and picture success

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: a hospital ethics chair preparing for a scarce-bed protocol
exampleSpecs.stakes: the first real crisis will arrive too fast for untested moral rules
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Ryan removes all patient names from three hypothetical cases and forces the board to choose by stated criteria before any real patient is waiting
exampleSpecs.firstImage: three blank case cards under a harsh meeting-room lamp

exampleSpecs.audience: a mission planner weighing whether to delay a small satellite launch
exampleSpecs.stakes: a rushed launch could waste years of lab work
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Manon asks the team to simulate the launch with the sensor fault unresolved and name the first irreversible loss before voting
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a red sensor flag blinking over a launch-window countdown

exampleSpecs.audience: a festival organizer considering a rain-or-shine policy
exampleSpecs.stakes: vendors could lose inventory and customers could crowd unsafe tents
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Tomas walks the planned festival in his mind during a thunderstorm and moves the ticket queue after noticing where wet people will bottleneck
exampleSpecs.firstImage: rainwater pooling in the chalk marks for the ticket line

exampleSpecs.audience: a ward manager redesigning discharge paperwork
exampleSpecs.stakes: patients may misunderstand medication instructions after leaving
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Anke pretend she is a tired patient with one bus transfer and test whether the new packet survives that path
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a discharge packet folded under a plastic pharmacy bag

exampleSpecs.audience: a field researcher planning a remote sampling season
exampleSpecs.stakes: a miscounted fuel cache could strand the team
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Akira writes a postmortem from the future where the camp runs short, then identifies the hidden assumption about generator hours
exampleSpecs.firstImage: frost on a fuel drum stencil at the edge of camp

exampleSpecs.audience: a conservatory dean testing blind audition procedures
exampleSpecs.stakes: a rule meant to increase fairness may create a new hidden advantage
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Isabel mentally runs the audition from the hallway, the sign-in desk, and the screen, then spots that accompanist access still reveals privilege
exampleSpecs.firstImage: numbered audition cards fanned beside a piano bench

skillTargets: detect hidden assumptions in a hypothetical
know when thought experiment must yield to real evidence

tryThisNowSpec: Choose one risky action. Run it once in your head with one fixed constraint, then write the first hidden assumption that appears.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
